summary: Erich Schmidt worked in linguistics, having studied at the universities of Graz, Strasbourg (under Wilhelm Scherer), and Jena. He held academic posts at the universities of Würzburg (1875–1877), Vienna (circa 1880–1887), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1887–1913).
Erik Braun is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun.

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. He later held academic positions at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (1951–1960), and Harvard University (circa 1960–1970).

Erik Haarh was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed a doctorate at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) and served as a department head and theology professor at Aarhus University (1969; 1983–1993).

Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University and served as an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director at Rangjung Yeshe Publications around 1980 and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark around 2004.

Erik Zürcher was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University, studying under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian who earned his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the University of Amsterdam (1993–1997), Leiden University (from 1997), and the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012).

Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied at the universities of Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, completing his PhD and habilitation at Cologne. He served as a professor of sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.

Ernest Arthur Gardner was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1880 to 1884. He later held an academic post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald. He held faculty posts at the University of Pennsylvania from 1950 to 1989.

Ernest Francisco Fenollosa worked in philosophy, Japanology, and art history after studying at Harvard. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1878), Tokyo National Museum (1888), Tokyo University of the Arts (1887–1890), and Boston's Museum of Fine Arts (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine from 1919 to 1922.

Ernest Renan was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Eugène Burnouf and Etienne Marc Quatremère. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France as Hebrew professor (1861) and director (1883).

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as a professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn, Göttingen, and Berlin under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, Christian August Brandis, Karl Otfried Müller, and August Boeckh. He held professorships at Berlin and Göttingen, and directed the Altes Museum (circa 1872–1896).

Ernst Förstemann was a linguist and historian who studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp. He served as librarian at the Fürstlich Stolberg-Wernigerödische Bibliothek (1851) and headed the Dresden library (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who habilitated at the University of Vienna. He held positions at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), the University of Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems (from 2007).

Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, where he studied under Albrecht Weber. He worked at the British Museum from 1866 and served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1875.

Ernst Johann Eitel was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his MA and PhD from the University of Tübingen. He served with the London Missionary Society (circa 1865–1879) and taught German at the University of Adelaide (circa 1897–1908).
